body.statement:
There is an explicitly parameterized nonempty relatively open subset \(\mathcal U\subset\mathcal M_0(2)\) and one may take \(\eta=1/5\) such that every law in \(\mathcal U\) satisfies
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})\ge\eta,
 \qquad H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0.
\]
Consequently the noncausal order \((Y,X)\) is a strict insertion-local maximizer of the exact \(\alpha=1\) population GENE score throughout \(\mathcal U\), although every law in \(\mathcal U\) identifies the causal order \(X\to Y\).
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 b(z)=c_b\exp\{-1/(1-z^2)\}\mathbf 1\{|z|<1\},
 \qquad m_2=\int z^2b(z)\,dz,
\]
and let \(\beta(t)=c_\beta\exp\{-1/[t(1-t)]\}\mathbf 1\{0<t<1\}\).  Put \(L=3\), \(\epsilon_\star=m_2/72\), and
\[
 v_\star=L^2\epsilon_\star(1-\epsilon_\star)>0.
\]
For \(0<h<1/2\) and \(0<\tau<1\), define on \([0,L]\)
\[
 p_{h,\tau}(x)
 =(1-\tau)\left\{(1-\epsilon_\star)h^{-1}\beta(x/h)
 +\epsilon_\star h^{-1}\beta((L-x)/h)\right\}+\frac{\tau}{L}. \tag{3}
\]
Terms involving \(\beta\) are understood as zero outside their displayed endpoint intervals.  Take \(X\) to have density (3), take \(N\) to have density \(b\), independently, and set \(Y=X+N\), with node domains \([0,3]\) and \([-1,4]\).

The densities in (3) and \(b\) are strictly positive and \(C^3\) on their relative interiors, the mechanism is smooth and nonconstant, and support closure is immediate.  The root support is connected.  To verify Condition 19, write \(\xi=\log p_{h,\tau}\), \(\nu=\log b\), and \(L_0(x,y)=\xi(x)+\nu(y-x)\).  A reverse ANM would force
\[
 \partial_x\{(L_0)_{xy}/(L_0)_{xx}\}=0. \tag{4}
\]
At \(y=x\), where \(\nu'''(0)=0\), the left side of (4) is nonzero at any point for which \(\xi'''(x)\ne0\) and \(\xi''(x)+\nu''(0)\ne0\).  Such a point exists: \(p_{h,\tau}\) is constant on \((h,L-h)\) but nonconstant on an endpoint interval, so \(\xi'''\) cannot vanish identically; and \(\xi''=-\nu''(0)\) cannot hold on every open set on which \(\xi'''\ne0\).  Continuity gives failure on an open patch.  Thus these laws satisfy all member properties of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\), including its Condition 19 restriction, and Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) identifies \(X\to Y\).

Couple \(X\) to \(X_0\in\{0,L\}\), with \(P(X_0=L)=\epsilon_\star\), by using the corresponding endpoint label on the first mixture term in (3), and any coupling on the bridge term.  Then
\[
 \mathbb E(X-X_0)^2\le B_{h,\tau}:=h^2+L^2\tau. \tag{5}
\]
The reverse triangle inequality in \(L^2\), applied after centering, gives
\[
 \left|\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(X)}-\sqrt{v_\star}\right|
 \le2\sqrt{B_{h,\tau}},
\]
and therefore \(|\operatorname{Var}(X)-v_\star|\le12\sqrt{B_{h,\tau}}\), since both variables lie in \([0,3]\).  Choose explicit positive \(h,\tau\) satisfying
\[
 B_{h,\tau}<\min\{v_\star/10,\ v_\star^2/2304\}. \tag{6}
\]
Then
\[
 \frac34v_\star<\operatorname{Var}(X)<\frac54v_\star.
\]
Because \(v_\star<m_2/8\), the forward correlation ratio obeys
\[
 q(Y,\{X\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)+m_2}
 <\frac15. \tag{7}
\]

For \(h<1/2\), the estimator \(\widehat X(Y)=0\) when \(Y<3/2\) and \(\widehat X(Y)=3\) otherwise classifies both endpoint components correctly.  Its squared error is at most \(h^2\) on those components and at most \(9\) on the bridge.  By conditional-mean optimality, (5)--(6) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)
 \le B_{h,\tau},
 \qquad
 q(X,\{Y\})
 =1-\frac{\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 >\frac{13}{15}. \tag{8}
\]
Combining (7) and (8) yields
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})
 >\frac{13}{30}-\frac15=\frac7{30}>\frac15. \tag{9}
\]

The reverse residual is dependent on \(Y\) for a support-geometric reason which is stable under perturbation.  At the displayed law,
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(X\mid Y=y)^{\circ}
 =\bigl(\max\{0,y-1\},\min\{3,y+1\}\bigr).
\]
On \(y\in(-1,1)\) its diameter is \(y+1\), which is not constant on a set of positive \(P_Y\)-measure.  Centering by \(\mathbb E[X\mid Y=y]\) only translates this support.  Independence of the centered residual and \(Y\) would require one common conditional support almost everywhere, a contradiction.  Characteristicness gives \(H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0\).

For completeness, define the structural topology by taking the graph discretely, the support endpoints in their Euclidean topology, mechanisms in \(C^1\), and compactly supported densities in \(L^1\) together with compact-open \(C^3\) convergence on relative interiors.  Around any parameter pair satisfying (6), impose the following strict primitive conditions: the mechanism is strictly increasing; the images of the two endpoint bands remain separated by more than the innovation-support diameter; the root mass outside those bands is small enough that the classifier bound divided by \(\operatorname{Var}(X)\) is less than \(1/5\); and
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}\{f(X)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{f(X)\}+\operatorname{Var}(N)}<\frac15.
\]
These are strict inequalities in structural functions, support endpoints, and density integrals, hence define a relatively open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) inside \(\mathcal M_0(2)\).  The same classifier proof gives \(q(X,\{Y\})>4/5\), and the last display gives \(q(Y,\{X\})<1/5\).  Strict monotonicity and full interior positivity make the diameter of the conditional-support interval vary near a support endpoint, so the reverse HSIC remains positive throughout \(\mathcal U\).  Thus (9), with the uniform choice \(\eta=1/5\), holds on \(\mathcal U\).  The independence indicator is not asserted to be continuous at zero: it is locally constant here only because the structural support argument supplies strict dependence.  Finally, the two possible orders have scores \(q(Y,\{X\})\) and \(q(X,\{Y\})/2\), so (9) makes the wrong order the unique insertion-local maximizer.
